findings.source_quote: προσκυνῶν ὑμᾶς καὶ θύων καὶ σπένδων καὶ τῆς ὑμετέρας μεταλαμβάνων τραπέζης ἢ ἕτερόν τι ὧν οὐ χρὴ ἐκτελῶν ἢ αἷμα χέων ἢ σαρκῶν νεκρῶν γευόμενος ἢ θηρίου λειψάνου ἢ τμητοῦ ἢ πνικτοῦ ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς ἀκαθάρτου ἐμπιπλάμενος
findings.english_quote: by worshiping you, sacrificing, pouring libations, partaking of your table, performing some other thing that ought not to be done, shedding blood, tasting dead flesh, or filling himself with what a wild animal has left, with something cut up, with something strangled, or with some other unclean thing
findings.issue: All listed actions are represented, but their connective structure is not. The Greek joins the first four ritual actions with repeated καί, then shifts to alternatives introduced by repeated ἤ. The English presents an undifferentiated list ending in “or,” concealing that distinction. The conjunctive wording here must not be flattened to match the disjunctive wording in 8.20.
findings.suggested_revision: Preserve the conjunctions explicitly: “by worshiping you and sacrificing and pouring libations and partaking of your table, or by performing some other thing that ought not to be done, or by shedding blood, or by tasting dead flesh, or by filling himself with what a wild animal has left, or with something cut up, or with something strangled, or with some other unclean thing.” This proposal retains the draft’s disclosed attachment and lexical choices; the revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: διὸ ἐξουσίαν τινὸς οὐκ ἔχει μὴ προσκυνήσαντος αὐτόν· ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ λαβεῖν τις παρ’ αὐτῶν δύναταί τι ὧν θέλει, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ βλαβῆναι οὐδέν
findings.english_quote: Therefore he has no authority over anyone who has not worshiped him. Nor can anyone receive from them anything he wants; neither can he be harmed at all
findings.issue: The scope of the final two denials is materially ambiguous and is not discussed in the notes. The indefinite τις can be read without an expressed restriction, as the draft does, but it can also contextually resume the preceding person who has not worshiped the ruler. That alternative limits both receiving benefits and suffering harm to the non-worshiper. The unrestricted rendering is grammatically defensible; the problem is undisclosed scope uncertainty, not source corruption or the mere existence of alternatives.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note explaining the contextual alternative: “Nor can such a person receive from them anything he wants; neither can he be harmed at all,” with “such a person” referring to someone who has not worshiped the ruler. If retaining the present main text, explain that it follows the unqualified indefinite τις as printed while acknowledging the possible contextual restriction. Any proposed change to the main text requires fresh review.
